title: Cat who hid in couch rescued from Saskatoon landfill
summary: Moze the cat had enough lives to survive an unscheduled trip to the dump in her favourite hiding spot.

image.caption: Moze, a four-year-old cat, was reunited with her owner Ryan Nitschke after hiding in a couch that was taken to the Saskatoon landfill. (Submitted by Alisha Visser)

blocks.text: Saskatoon
Moze the cat had enough lives to survive an unscheduled trip to the dump in her favourite hiding spot.
'She is completely unharmed, unscathed and no injuries,' says owner of Moze, 4
A Saskatoon couple is happy their four-year-old cat, Moze, had enough of her nine lives left to survive an unexpected trip to the landfill inside her favourite hiding spot in a couch.
The ordeal started in October when Ryan Nitschke and Alisha Vessir had a couch and love seat moved out of their home to make space for new furniture.

“Like an hour later, my girlfriend and I were lying in bed and we were saying, ‘I wonder when Moze is going to reappear.’ She always hides whenever we have visitors. She hates company," Nitschke said. "Then it occurred to us that her favourite place is inside the couch.”
Moze, a four-year-old cat, was reunited with her owners after hiding in a couch and ending up in the Saskatoon landfill. (Submitted by Alisha Vessir)
In a panic, Nitschke got into the car and drove to the landfill.

“I explained the situation. We drove around and up to the top of the hill where they crush and compact the trash. Luckily, we didn't see any signs of the couches there. So we went down to the bins where it gets dropped off, and like, as we were driving up, they were hooking up the bin that had our couches.”
Matt Cuthbertson works at the material recovery centre. He said everything fell perfectly into place to find Moze.

“Normally I take a late lunch, which means I probably would have grabbed the full bins and taken them up top,” he said. “But I took an early lunch and when I was coming back, as I was hooking up to a bin, I heard over the radio, Johnny my manager, he’s like ‘don’t grab any bins. I’ll be right there.'”

Cuthbertson, who describes himself as a cat person, said it hit home.
“When I initially heard this, my stomach dropped, and I was pretty devastated. But also that adrenaline of like, if it’s here, we've got to find this cat,” he said.
The crew found Nitscke’s furniture in the bin and began cutting into the couches.
Cuthbertson said they didn’t see any sign of Moze at first, but kept going.
“We're fiddling around, kind of looking for every nook and cranny,” he said. “All of a sudden, yeah, Johnny's like, 'I see it.'”
Moze was curled up inside the couch's armrest. All the workers could see was belly, fur and eyes.
“Perfect happy ending. The fact that we didn’t give up after, and Johnny’s eagle eyes, he saved us. I just felt this joy," Cuthbertson said. "It was a beautiful thing.”
How this Sask. cat accidentally took a trip to the dump
Nitschke is amazed that everything turned out so well and thankful that everyone at the landfill went the extra mile to help.
“There were so many opportunities for the worst to happen. But she is completely unharmed, unscathed and no injuries,” Nitschke said.
"She was a little scared when she got home, but by the end of the night she was back to her usual self."
A thank you note for the landfill crew who helped rescue Moze. (Submitted by the City of Saskatoon)
